title: Cmd-N, then Ctrl-` AT ONCE (no wait for the workspace to show), then type: the line runs in the new terminal at once
why: STATUS 1729: in 6 of 14 rounds of focus-switch-corner-drag the line typed after Cmd-N then Ctrl-` got debug.key handled_by app (the router's stale last action newSurface) and did not run. Cmd-N's New Tab key hold owns every key of its window until its page reports ready (at most 4 s); a Ctrl-` before that hid the page and the hold kept the keys typed for the new terminal. The last check records the New Tab hold's log (debug.focus new_tab_key_log): 'hold key' on the base, 'release: a creation took the keys' on the fix, when the page was not ready at the Ctrl-` (the hold path). QUICK VARIANT (journey parameter, coordinator rule 2026-10-31): the only change from cmdn-ctrlbt-type is that the Ctrl-` follows Cmd-N's reply at once instead of after the 'new workspace shows' expect (about 60-150 ms later), so the Ctrl-` comes before the New Tab page's readiness (113-275 ms) more often and more rounds take the hold path. Run on the base and the head builds the same way. A refused Ctrl-` (a pane still opening) fails before the final expect: 'not run'.
source: P0 CMD-N CTRL-BACKTICK FIRST KEY (STATUS 1729), agent a539d1ff2011e6d9e
